# TODO.md — the persistent source of truth

This file is how work resumes after a context compaction, a restart, or a new
agent. Tick items as they finish. Add categories as plans land. If a task is not
here, add it and tick it. Implementation details do not belong here — only tasks
worth tracking.

Legend: `[ ]` pending · `[~]` in progress · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked · `[-]` cancelled

### Icons (`@gpuixui/icons`)

`[x]` `[██████████]` 2/2

`[x]` Read a **stored size name as the default step, not a vanished box** —
`Icon`'s `size` and `Spinner`'s dot side both resolve through `iconPixels`, and
its name branch was a bare `ICON_SIZES[size]`: `size` is a stored preference as
often as a literal, so a name from a release that renamed or dropped a step
arrives as a string the union no longer names, and the lookup answered
`undefined`. `Icon` wrote that to `style.width`/`style.height`, and the runtime
paints a sized SVG with no side as a **full-width, zero-height** box — measured
in a window at **1256 × 0** inside a 1280px frame — so a toolbar row around a
vanished glyph stretched across the window. `iconPixels` now takes the decoded
value as `unknown` (the rule `revealFrames` follows) and reads a name the scale
does not carry as the `md` step, beside the numeric rule it already had;
`isIconSize` is the membership test, derived from `ICON_SIZES` rather than a
second list. `sizes.test.ts` gains `reads a name the scale does not carry as the
default step` and `runtime/icons.runtime.test.tsx`
`paints an icon whose stored size name the scale no longer carries`; directions
measured: with the bare lookup restored, the unit case fails
`expected undefined to be 16` and the window case `expected 16, got 1256`.
Docs: `packages/icons/docs/icon.mdx` §Sizes (held by `docs.test.ts`'s
`teaches the answer a stored size name gets`, which pairs the words with the
resolver's own answer), the icons README §Sizes and

### Design tokens and theming (`tokens-theme`)

`[x]` `[██████████]` 212/212

`[x]` Search the **accent's ladder lazily**, and hold it to the smallest step —
`nativeAccent` walked the whole 2% ladder before choosing a rung
(`Array.from({ length: 51 }, …).find(carries)`), so every call blended all 51
colours even when the brand's own `primary` already carried the mark: `nativeTextTheme`
calls it, and a field or code host calls that on every render, so a paint-path
helper cost 51 × four surfaces × two ratios per field. The rung is now found over
indices with the blend inside the predicate, so a theme that needs no step costs
**one** blend and a stepped one costs its own rung: measured in one process, 500
`nativeAccent` calls on the base dark theme went **832 → 216 ms** and the base light
theme (which does step) 1 268 → 1 118 ms. The promise the JSDoc makes — "the
**smallest** 2% step whose marker composite clears" — was held by nothing: the suite
measured only "the brand was not enough" and "the result clears", so a search that
started above the brand or over-shot into the ink passed. `native-text.test.ts` gains
`steps by the smallest share that clears, never past it`, which re-derives the first
carrying rung per style from the floors and the two shares and requires the resolved
colour to be exactly it (the granularity is read from the source, so a changed step
count fails until the case moves). Directions measured: a search that starts at step
1 fails four cases by name, the new one included. Docs already state the smallest
step; no page changes. No native scenario applies — a pure derivation.

`[x]` Keep the **role and level sweeps inside the suite's own budget** — the broad
guards a role or an elevation level added to a theme must pass without a new case
(`incomplete.test.ts`'s role and level sweeps and `native-text.test.ts`'s "never
throws for a role any shipped style lost") ran a whole `auditTheme` **per role and per
level** — 752, 846 and 72 audits, eleven reports each — and asked for a twenty-second
timeout to do it: **29.7 s** on a full-suite run against the package's deliberate
two-second budget, so master's tokens gate was red on a loaded box (`Test timed out in
20000ms`, measured twice on 2026-10-23). None of the claims needs the other nine
reports: the role sweep reads `invalidColorRoles` (the role named once) and the pairs
that name the role out of `contrastPairs`/`contrastRatio` (none readable), the level
sweep reads `invalidShadowColors`, and the seam sweep reads `nativeTextTheme` for both
fills over the 47 roles (the seam's answer to an absent role is the same code in every
palette; the palette dimension is the complete-theme sweep and `nativeAccent`'s own
shipped-style case). `passed`, the no-throw rule and the whole-group superset stay
where they already live (`audit.test.ts`'s conjunction case and `incomplete.test.ts`'s
absent-group cases). **The gate is read once per style**: five cases asked whether
every shipped style passes and each paid for eighteen audits (~750 ms apiece), so
`shippedAudits` is built at module load and each case keeps its own claim; the font
case reads `missingTokens`, which is the list the refusal is built from. Every
twenty-second exemption is gone, so the suite's two seconds is the guard: the package
is 49 files / **2 933 tests in 8.7 s** (was 35.6 s with two failures), and the file's
slowest case went 2 897 ms → **57 ms**. Directions measured: `themeColors` filling an
absent role from `lightColors` fails the role sweep by name (846 rows), skipping a

A theme owns a palette by carrying `syntax`, which **replaces the table whole** (a complete palette is what the host reads; a brand spreads `syntaxColors(theme)` to edit one token — `Partial<Record<…>>` cannot accept an object literal here because TypeScript's inherited `Object.constructor` collides with the runtime's `constructor` token), and a `PlatformStyle` may declare one per mode, which `applyStyle` hands over under its palette rule. **Adopted with no component change**: the components package's `CodeBlock` passes `nativeTextTheme(theme, "background")`, and the seam now hands `syntaxColors(theme)` to the host. `syntax.test.ts` (12 cases) holds the tables, the 672-placement sweep over the 14 shipped, platform and look themes, the tightest cell (dark `keyword` on Linux's page, **7.22:1**), the resolution, the brand and style routes, the erased keyword, the unmeasurable `hsl()` token and the executed example; `catalogue-values.test.ts` holds the printed table (24 rows × two columns), the four table names, the two high-contrast comment values and the printed tightest to the exports. Directions measured: removing `syntax: syntaxColors(theme)` fails three cases by name in `syntax.test.ts`/`native-text.test.ts`, dropping the `syntax` half of `passed` fails `reports a token that vanishes into the page`, painting the light `keyword` as the page fails the sweep and the printed row, and a printed `#3B2C91` fails the catalogue case. Docs: `docs/tokens.md` §Syntax palette (table, floors, brand and look routes, the retracted limitation), `docs/design-system.md` §9, the package README and the **Syntax palette** inventory row. The painted pixels are the interlock below

Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Paint-ready values and `docs/design-system.md` §9 now state the refusal and quote the message.

Four pairs joined `contrastPairs` (93 → 97) at the boundary floor, and the values moved by the smallest step that clears all four tints — light `#727D8C` → `#6A7483`, dark `#788494` → `#949EAB`, high-contrast light `#4A4F58` → `#454A53`, macOS light `#7C7C82` → `#75757A` and dark `#8A8A90` → `#9C9CA1`, Linux light `#7E7C79` → `#76746F`, Windows dark `#9A9A9A` → `#9D9D9D`, Luna dark `#7E9CBF` → `#83A1C3`, Aero light `#5E7A93` → `#5A768F` and dark `#7F98AC` → `#889FB2`. `contrast.test.ts`'s `a control's edge on a message's own tint` suite holds the coverage, reads the alert's tones, its description and the default action's edge so the pairs cannot outlive the paint, reports an edge painted in the tint it sits on at 1.00:1, sweeps all 16 styles to the printed 3.09 (macOS light's red tint) and reads the catalogue's sentence; `catalogue-values.test.ts` holds every moved value the page prints. Directions measured: restoring `xl: 8` fails the shipped sweep and the `xl > lg` case (2 red), and `invalidScales` returning `[]` fails 5 cases by name. `[x]` Decide the gate's behaviour on an **incomplete theme** — `docs/tokens.md` §Paint-ready values promised that "a role missing from a hand-built theme literal is reported too", and the reports instead threw: `invalidColorRoles` read `value.trim()` on `undefined` and `invalidShadowColors` crashed on a level that was absent. That is exactly the shape a theme restored from storage has when it predates a role the library added since — the one way a complete theme becomes incomplete. **Decision: absence is a value the report carries, not an exception.** `isPaintableColor` takes `unknown` and answers `false` for anything that is not a string (a decoded value can be absent, a number or `null`); `invalidColorRoles` takes `Partial<ThemeColors>` and reports the role with `value: undefined`; `invalidShadowColors` takes `Partial<Elevation>` and reports an absent level once, at position `0`, with `color: undefined` (empty `overlay` still reports nothing). The contracts that measure a pair take the same colour source — `contrastFailures`, `decorativeFailures`, `indicatorFailures`, `seriesFailures`, `disabledFadeFailures`, `keyboardDimFailures`, `selectionFailures` (whose `wash` may now be absent) and `fadedPair` — and a pair they cannot compose is reported **unmeasurable** rather than skipped, so `auditTheme` names the missing role and fails `passed` instead of throwing; `NumberSource` reads the levels a theme carries, because a numeric group is a breaking change while a role is additive. `incomplete.test.ts` (8 cases) removes every role and every elevation level from all 16 shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored themes and asserts the gate names it, the pairs touching it stay unmeasurable, and nothing throws; it also holds the total paint check, the documentation order, the single-role case and a complete theme still passing. Both directions measured: restoring `value.trim()` fails 4 cases with the `TypeError`, and dropping the absent-level branch fails the level report and the 16-theme sweep. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Paint-ready values/§Checking your own theme, `docs/design-system.md` §9/§11, the package README and the `Colour grammar`/`Elevation` inventory rows.

`[x]` Measure the **shadow a raised surface drops** — the one surface both pages said was *deliberately* outside the contract ("a shadow is a blurred geometry, so a flat composite would overstate it"), and the exemption hid a real defect: the high-contrast dark theme tints its shadows with black (`highContrastDarkColors.shadow` was `#000000B3`) on a **pure-black page**, so every level measured 1.00:1 on `background` and a dialog or a full-width card in that variant had no shadow at all. **Decision: measure it as a ceiling.** `DecorativeSurface` gains `surface: "elevation"` with a `level`, the painted colour is the **level's own** (a level carries its share in its alpha byte, and a brand can supply one whole), and the table measures the scale's **deepest** step (`lg`) over the four strips a raised surface falls on (`background`, `card`, `popover`, `muted`) at `decorativeFloor`. `[x]` Decide **where the selection wash is painted** — `selectionPairs` measured the content tones and the primitives' `surfaceStyle` also paints `accent` and `selected`, so a selectable `Text` inside either one was washed with nothing measuring it. It cannot be measured, and the reason is structural rather than a gap: the wash is a share of the accent family and both tones are drawn from the same family, so a selection moves the fill *toward* its text instead of away from it. Measured over the sixteen shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored styles, the wash costs contrast in **all 80 placements** on those two tones — it never once helps — and leaves **26 of the 80 under the floor the unwashed pair already met** (tightest: Windows XP (Luna) dark's secondary line on a selected row at **3.78:1**, its body text on the same fill at **5.54:1**). No share can serve both jobs: one strong enough to be seen on the page is what erases text on a saturated fill, and one weak enough there is invisible on the page. **Decision: a selectable run belongs on a content tone**, the two saturated tones stay outside `selectionPairs`, and a state row that needs selectable text paints it on a content tone. The exclusion is measured, not assumed: `selection.test.ts`'s `the tones the wash is painted on` suite derives the box's own `SURFACE_TONES` from the primitives (a tone added there is unmeasured until this suite is told, proven with a planted `secondary`), holds all 80 placements so a palette that made the wash *help* fails until the decision is re-read, and prints the count and both tightest ratios on `docs/tokens.md`, `docs/design-system.md`, the README and the `Text selection wash` row.       `<svg>` paint a wide generated path scaled and clipped to its box, and how
      does it react to a resize? The `svg-pattern` live probe answers it on
      0.11.0 with five shapes of disjoint tints in one frame. A **200×200**
      square (a 60-unit square stroked 10 in a 100-unit view box) paints
      **140×140**: the path is scaled 2× with its stroke and centred. A band
      drawn from −40 to 140 is clipped at the view box's edge — **200** wide,
      **40** tall, nothing outside. The same band in a **300×100** box paints
      **300** wide and **30** thick, while in a **100×200** box it paints **100**
      wide and **10** thick: the scale is the element's **width** alone (the
      height is never consulted), a stroke's weight follows it, and the content
      is centred instead of fitted or stretched. One `<path>` of **20** subpaths
      paints **20/20** at each stroke's centre. A press resizing the square to
      300×100 lays the path out again at **210** wide, and the square content
      area (300 tall) paints **above and below** the 100-point element — the
      element does not clip it, so a hexagon or topography field must be sized
      near-square or its line art bleeds onto whatever is painted after it.
      34 checks, `--only svg-pattern`, green (~1.9 s). Four negative controls
      measured (exit `1`, restored green): dropping the stroke from the expected
      fraction fails `expected 120 ± 4, got 140`; truncating the generated path
      by one subpath fails `expected 20, got 19`; drawing the band inside the
      view box fails `expected 200 ± 3, got 160`; resizing to a square box fails
      `expected true, got false`. Fixture: `src/live/pattern.ts` +
      `pattern.test.ts` (9 cases). `registry.test.ts` now partitions the
      registry across the full pass, its reds and the probes measured alone
      since (three directions measured: an unaccounted probe, a dropped red and
      an unregistered id each fail by count). Evidence:
      `apps/playground/README.md` §`svg-pattern`,
      `.artifacts/live/svg-pattern{,-resized}.png`. The components half stays the
      `hexagon, topography` row in plan 600's section.

      `aria-id` reach `label`/`description`/`author_id`;

      `selected`/`expanded`/`level`/`value`; `onClick`+`tabIndex` surface as the

      **a node needs a role to exist at all** — a div carrying only an
      `aria-label` paints no node and `role="none"` is dropped. 19 checks,
      `--only a11y-tree`, green on 0.11.0; full headless suite re-run 38/38. Two
      negative controls measured (dropping the button's `role`: `the tree
      describes "Save project" — expected a value, got none`; dropping its
      `aria-description`: `aria-description reaches the tree — expected "Writes
      the file", got ""`, exit `1` each). Evidence:

      only for the first paint would make the workaround useless. A 560px row of
      a 120px sidebar, a flexible centre and a fixed 100px inspector; `Widen
      sidebar` takes 100px from the centre. Measured on 0.11.0: the commit's
      layout pass arrives **before** the new width applies and reports the box

      the next frame and equals the pane's painted `bounds`; the 100px inspector
      keeps its box and **still receives a report** (its count reaches 2); and
      narrowing reports the original 340 again. So the signal exists, but a
      report is not a "you changed" event — a stale pass arrives first and an
      unchanged pane is reported to — so a re-clamp acts on the width the payload
      carries and is idempotent. 12 checks, `--only dock-reflow`, green on
      0.11.0 (the counts behind it re-run three times); full headless suite
      re-run 37/37. Two negative controls measured (a centre that does not flex:

`@gpuix/native@0.10.0` published only `-darwin-arm64`, `-linux-x64-gnu`,
`-win32-x64-msvc`; loading it failed with `mach-o file, but is an incompatible
architecture (have 'arm64', need 'x86_64')`.

Still true and worth remembering:

- The `wasm` build exports only `GpuixRenderer`, not `TestGpuixRenderer`.
- The binding is a **locally built artifact**, not a published one: a clean
  `nub install` on a bare host still has none, so the behaviour suites stay out
  of the default `test` run (plan 117 §5a–§5c) and a host without a binding
  reports `unsupported-host` from `src/runtime.test.tsx`.
- On an Apple-silicon Mac, Linux x64 or Windows x64 the published binding works
  with no local build.

Consequences for Tier 2: Escape dismissal, layer stacking, focus-in/out and
Tab trapping must be implemented in this package on top of `renderer.focusElement`
/ `focusNextWithin` / `focusPreviousWithin` and element-level `onKeyDown`, instead
of relying on the clone's `DismissableLayer`. `Button`/`buttonProps` and
`Dialog` parts must be equivalent local implementations over `<div>` + host props
until `packages/primitives` and a newer `@gpuix/react` land. Plans 110 §1/§7 and
112/114 have been corrected for this.

Related: the reference clone must not be treated as the API of the pinned
dependency anywhere in this repo, and `package.json` pins must stay explicit.

  - [x] **Virtualized hierarchical data** — `@gpuixui/data` ships `VirtualTree`:
    the tree's flattening, cursor and keyboard over the runtime's `itemCount`
    window, so a 4 000-row hierarchy retains and paints only the rows around the
    viewport. `tree/row` and `tree/use-tree` are the one row paint and keyboard
    controller both trees share, so the inset, type-ahead, chevron press rule and
    reveal focus cannot drift. Four measured rules are in the composition: a
    cursor move mounts its row before the focus moves; a reveal moves the window
    before the scroll; the window follows `getListScrollTop`, not the lagging
    `onVisibleRange`; and a mounted tab stop always exists — a wheel or collapse
    that unmounts the cursor's row moves the cursor to the viewport's top row,
    focusing it only when the tree held the focus. 7 native behaviour cases mount
    the 40-directory × 99-file example: only a window is retained in React (the
    far row is in neither `getAllText` nor the frame), expand-all makes 4 000
    rows, `End` moves the window then focuses the last row, a caller's reveal
    re-takes the focus after the press, a wheel leaves a mounted focused tab
    stop, `Right` expands in place, and a collapse that hides the cursor's row
    keeps a live keyboard stop. Docs `packages/data/docs/virtual-tree.mdx`;
    example `virtual-tree.example.tsx`. Owner: data.

`[x]` `@gpuixui/motion`: **an interpolation overflowed between two readable values** — every sampler promised to replace a number it cannot read, but the two interpolators added a **difference**: `MotionValue`'s tween computed `from + (target - from) * progress` and `sampleKeyframes` did the same for a segment, so two finite endpoints whose difference overflows painted a frame the runtime draws as nothing — a tween from `-1e308` to `1e308` answered `NaN` at its first frame (`Infinity * 0`), `Infinity` at every later one, and only appeared at the target; the keyframe segment did both in one run. A bound now stops a coast only when the coast moves into it (the floor with a non-positive velocity, the ceiling with a non-negative one); the interior path, the clamp-at-the-wall stop and the settle against a wall are unchanged. Proof: `inertia.test.ts`'s `a coast released on a wall` (2 cases: both directions leave the wall with their velocity and are inside the range on the next sample, while a release pushing into the wall still settles at zero) and `motion.test.ts`'s `keeps a coast released on a wall travelling back into its range` (the retained value's release sample stays at `20`, active and not complete, and its 100 ms sample is inside the range). Directions measured: at `HEAD` the sampler answers `{ value: 0, velocity: 0, settled: true }` and the retained value reads `0` where `20` is required; with the rule, 12 files / 125 tests green, `check-types`, lint and fmt clean. Docs: the module and `sampleInertia` JSDoc, `packages/motion/README.md` §Inputs the runtime can paint.

The absent object is read as `{}` now — the house spring, the answer every unreadable field already gets — so `springPhysics`, `atRest`, `sampleSpring` and the retained value are total through that door. Proof: `spring.test.ts`'s `reads a declaration that carries no physics as the house spring` and `motion.test.ts`'s `animates a spring declaration that carries no physics` (a middle sample strictly between `0` and `1`, then the exact target with `complete`); directions measured with the old `physicsOf` restored, where both fail on the exact `TypeError` (`undefined` for the transition, `null` for the constructor). Restored: 14 files / 159 tests, `check-types` and `lint` clean. Docs: the `physicsOf` JSDoc and `packages/motion/README.md` §Inputs the runtime can paint. `[x]` `@gpuixui/motion`: **a frame list was read as if it were already ascending** — `sampleKeyframes` took `stops[0]` and the last entry as the set's ends and then `findIndex`-ed for the first stop at or above the progress, so the sampler's answer depended on the order a caller declared the frames in: a list built from a map or a decoded config (JavaScript iterates integer-like keys first) answered the **first-declared** frame for every progress below its offset — `[0.8 → 1, 0.2 → 0]` at `0.1` returned `1` instead of `0`, a step function in place of the journey — while the JSDoc and `/docs/motion` made "sorted ascending" the caller's obligation and nothing checked it.
